_comment: Department of Basic Education Grade 10 Mathematics P2 (statistics, analytical geometry, trigonometry, measurement and Euclidean geometry), November 2019 national common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers transcribed from the rendered pages of the official PDFs
(paper2.pdf, paper2_memo.pdf); the text layer does not hold usable equations. Notation:
^ for powers, sqrt() for roots, a/b for fractions, decimal commas as printed. memo_answer is the
guideline's final answer and memo_working its working (tick marks and mark descriptors left out).
The guideline is bilingual (English/Afrikaans); only the English is transcribed. Graphs and diagrams are described
in brackets in the question text. The information sheet printed with the paper is not transcribed.
Both PDFs were obtained from the Eastern Cape Department of Education exam archive (source_url); the
page headers read 'DBE/November 2019' and 'CAPS - Grade 10', i.e. this is the national DBE paper
written in the province. The question paper is a scan with no text layer.
FORMAT: 100 marks, 2 hours, eight compulsory questions (Q1 16, Q2 15, Q3 15, Q4 16, Q5 8, Q6 9, Q7 9,
Q8 12). Candidates answer in a SPECIAL ANSWER BOOK (paper2_answer_book.pdf) that holds the scaled line

questions.context: QUESTION 7 | Give reasons for ALL geometry statements used in QUESTIONS 7 and 8. 7.1 In the diagram, EFGH is a rectangle having diagonals intersecting at M. M̂2 = 60° and L̂2 = 40°. [K and L lie on HG; MK and ML are drawn; M̂2 = EM̂H, M̂1 = FM̂G and M̂3 = KM̂L; F̂1 = EF̂M; L̂2 = ML̂K.] Calculate the size of:
questions.memo_working: EM̂F = 120° [∠s on a straight line]; F̂1 = Ê1 = 30° [∠s opp. = sides; diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other]

questions.text: GM̂L
questions.memo_working: Ê1 = Ĝ1 = 30° [alt. ∠s, EF ∥ HG]; L̂2 = Ĝ1 + GM̂L [ext. ∠ of Δ]; 40° = 30° + GM̂L

questions.context: 7.2 PQRS is a rhombus with diagonals PR and SQ intersecting at M. The perimeter of the rhombus is 12 cm. L is the midpoint of PS.
questions.text: Calculate the length of LM.
questions.memo_working: one side = 12/4 = 3 cm, so SR = 3 cm; PM = MR [diagonals of rhombus]; PL = LS [given]; in ΔPSR LM = 1/2 SR [midpoint theorem]

questions.text: Complete the statement so that it is TRUE: The diagonals of a parallelogram ... each other.

questions.context: 8.2 In the diagram below, P is the midpoint of side WQ of ΔWQR. V is on WR such that VP ∥ RQ. PV is produced by its own length to S. PW is produced to T and ST drawn.
questions.text: Give a reason why WV = VR.
questions.memo_answer: A line drawn from the midpoint of one side of a triangle parallel to another side bisects the third side.

questions.text: ΔVWP ≡ ΔVRS
questions.memo_answer: In ΔVWP and ΔVRS: WV = VR [proved]; VP = SV [given]; V̂1 = V̂3 [vert. opp. ∠s]; ΔVWP ≡ ΔVRS [SAS]

questions.text: SWPR is a parallelogram
questions.memo_answer: WV = VR [proved] and VP = SV [given], so SWPR is a parallelogram [diagonals bisect each other]

questions.text: PQRS is a parallelogram
questions.memo_answer: PQ ∥ SR (WP ∥ SR) and SP ∥ RQ [given]: PQRS is a parallelogram [both pairs of opp. sides ∥]. OR PQ ∥ SR and PQ = SR (PQ = WP = SR): one pair of opp. sides equal and ∥

questions.text: If it is further given that RSTW is a parallelogram, show that TQ = 3SR.
questions.memo_working: SR = TW [RSTW is a parallelogram]; SR = WP [proved]; WP = QP [given]; TQ = TW + WP + PQ = 3SR
